claim: ADR-0008 r3's 'Same scope as v1' table lists only the bare 'user permissions.deny -> deny' row and never names ctx_execute, ctx_execute_file or ctx_batch_execute. v1 enforced the same deny rules against those tools at both hook and server layers; a Bash(rm -rf:*) deny is otherwise bypassed by routing the same command through ctx_execute.
proof: Re-read docs/v2/adr/0008-enforcement-rewrite-and-cap.md lines 8-16: the scope table's rows are WebFetch, curl/wget, inline HTTP, build tools, Read>50KB, Grep/Bash hint, and user permissions.deny only; a repo-wide grep for ctx_execute/ctx_execute_file/ctx_batch_execute in that file matches only the build-tool alternative and issue #1269's alternative, never a scope-table row, so the gap is real.

claim: Change #2's 'allow when the body does not reach stdout' test drops v1's silent-flag and verbose-flag conditions for issue #166. 'curl -o f url' (no -s) and 'curl -s --verbose -o f url' would now be allowed, re-breaking the stderr progress-bar flood #166 fixed.
proof: Re-read the change-#2 row (line 25) and the GP3 golden-case table (lines 55-67): the rule text only checks where the body goes (file vs stdout) with no verbose/silent condition, and GP3 tests only the silent case 'curl -sL -o out.bin' as allow; no row tests a non-silent or --verbose file-output curl, so the no-silent/verbose gap from #166 is still open.

claim: Case B's PreToolUse 'allow' + updatedInput on a subagent Bash call means Claude Code skips the permission prompt entirely, and the rewritten command becomes 'node <bundle>/run.mjs <base64>', so any Bash(...) deny/ask rule and any other hook that inspects the command text no longer sees the real command.
proof: Re-read ADR-0016 line 27 and the whole doc: case B is described only as rewrite-then-run, with no step that runs the original command through ADR-0008's deny/ask checks first; ADR-0008 itself has no cross-reference to ADR-0016's rewrite path, so no text in either ADR requires checking the original command before issuing the allow+updatedInput rewrite.

claim: P1299 'hooks: route quoted curl/wget stdout destinations' is marked 'v2 hook routing must keep this as a contract test', but no ADR (0001-0016) or TECH-SPEC section names a quoted-argument parsing rule for the curl/wget interceptor, so the contract test has no spec to assert against.
proof: docs/v2/TECH-SPEC.md:267 lists '#1299: quoted curl/wget destinations -> GP3' and TECH-SPEC.md:289's GP3 row states the pass criteria 'PowerShell and quoted curl/wget routed', so the contract test does have a named spec to assert against; the original claim's grep missed TECH-SPEC.md.
